item.title: Wireless networks and schools
item.description: I spent pretty much the whole part of 2025 optimising the wireless network in my school. Most schools don’t have the technical expertise after the initial deployment to optimise the install; they are wholly dependent on the main vendor to configure everything. I find this a hit and miss scenario - most schools are left on the default configuration and untouched after that. After all, they could always call in to the hotline to get configurations changed. Unfortunately, most wouldn’t know how to describe the problem properly and if so, users complaining about wireless will almost always complain about 1 thing : speed.

item.title: Google ChromeOS updates
item.description:
Ever spent a long time chasing your tail and when you finally discover the solution, there is a sense of achievement? I felt like that today.

This effort involved troubleshooting a particular piece of software (that runs on Chromebooks) which the school uses to conduct exams. It worked for the most part but all of a sudden, students started reporting failures. I was suspicious of network changes but a call to the vendors cleared that up - there were no changes made to the firewall.
